answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit work, then randomly assigning bonded agents to verify one another’s outputs. If a randomly selected verifier approves demonstrably false work, a challenge can trigger evidence-based slashing of its bond; repeated identities do not multiply influence without multiplying capital at risk. An attacker must fund many independent stakes and risk losing them, while the oasis, umber, and terrace tasks still need to pass checks.
